text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Finance Minister Theo Waigel opposed delay of European economic and monetary union (EMU). Speculation about when France might join EMU. Bonn has 70 billion marks in new debt
- The office which replaced Germany's Treuhand organisation responsible for privatisation in former communist East Germany will finish its work by the end of 1999.
- Increasing numbers of large enterprises change owners
- The surface of the planet Mars is explored for the first time
HANDELSBLATT

- Bavaria continues row over how strictly to interpret the entry criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU). After an exchange of blows over the decimal point Munich renews it battle with Bonn as champion of a hard euro, Europe's planned single currency

- Germany's liberal Free Democrats (FDP) rule out tax increases in negotiations in parliamentary mediation committee over Chancellor Helmut Kohl's tax reform bill, which was rejected last week by the Bundesrat upper house of parliament
- Siemens chief Heinrich von Pierer calls for more help for Russia's nuclear power stations
- The Netherlands is interested in Transrapid high-speed railway link from Hamburg to Groningen
- Social Democrat social expert Rudolf Dressler calls for examination of doctor's accounting system after allegations that bills from heart disease clinics had been manipulated
- Pro-Sieben television shares floated at 72 marks. The inital public offering was over 50 times oversubscribed
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- NASA robots explore the surface of the planet Mars
- Defence Minister Volker Ruehe threatens with prosecution soldiers who staged mock executions with each other and filmed them. All those who took part in videos have been identified

- Bavaria's Christian Social Union (CSU), sister party to Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, locked in row over euro. Finance Minister Theo Waigel, who is the CSU chief, ruled out launching European economic and monetary union (EMU) without France
- German Agricultural Minister Jochen Borchert says German farmers need the euro
DIE WELT
- Doubts about launch of euro planned for 1999 grow. Finance Minister Theo Waigel confirms new debt. France says it will over step deficit criterium
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl rejects church criticism
- Germans are sceptical about the euro. European citizens feel they are not informed enough about the euro
- Pro-Sieben shares are 50-times oversubscribed and are floated at 72 marks.
